articles.summary: NEW DELHI: BJP allies in the party-led ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) on Saturday welcomed the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) statement
articles.body: NEW DELHI: BJP allies in the party-led ruling National Democratic Alliance (NDA) on Saturday welcomed the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) statement in response to a media report claiming a “rift” between Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and the two Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise.Also Read | 'Truth has come to light': BJP after EC clarifies 'no rift' over electoral roll revision"In the recent months, the Commission has taken numerous decisions including SIR across the country. The order for the SIR issued on 24.6.2025 for all the States/UTs, starting with Bihar, followed by West Bengal and 30 other States/UTs was issued with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The same has been upheld by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India vide its order dated 27.5.2026. The schedule for SIR for 12 States and UTs was issued on 27.10.2025 and those for 19 States/UTs was issued on 14.05.2026 with the unanimous approval of the Commission. The final figure of number of electors will be known only after final publication in the remaining 12 states of Phase-III," the ECI's press note read.Following the ECI's statement, Union minister and Lok Janshakti Party (LJP) chief Chirag Paswan, among the first BJP allies to raise the issue, maintained that it was his responsibility to voice any question or concern arising in the public mind.Also Read | 'Avoids issue of Gen Z voters': Congress attacks EC's 'wishy-washy' press note, seeks pause in SIR“The concerns raised by the public regarding SIR, which came before us, were presented before the Election Commission... Today, the Election Commission has clearly stated its position on all important issues point by point. The process of SIR, the unanimous agreement of all three commissioners, and the facts related to the meeting with the Cabinet Secretary have also been clearly presented,” Paswan posted in Hindi on X.“This clarity further strengthens public trust in democracy. The Election Commission plays a crucial role in democracy, and in this way, the trust of the country's people in democracy has increased even more,” the Hajipur MP added.Andhra Pradesh chief minister and Telugu Desam Party (TDP) supremo N Chandrababu Naidu also welcomed the Election Commission’s statement, maintaining that it "reaffirmed the credibility of constitutional institutions."“Attempts to undermine global confidence in India’s democratic framework or electoral processes for short-term political gains are deeply unfortunate. Electoral outcomes reflect the people’s mandate. In a robust democracy, leadership also means accepting both victories and defeats with grace and humility. Respect for our constitutional institutions is paramount. It is the collective responsibility of leaders across party lines to uphold public confidence in India’s democratic process,” Naidu wrote.BJP national president Nitin Nabin, too, slammed at the Congress-led opposition INDIA bloc for "misleading" the public on SIR.NDA constituents such as the LJP, TDP, Rashtriya Lok Morcha, and Janata Dal (Secular), had sought a detailed response from the ECI over The Indian Express report that Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi had objected at least 14 times over 10 months to decisions and orders related to the electoral roll revision process, reflecting the unease within the ruling alliance.Meanwhile, opposition parties, including the Congress, Samajwadi Party, Rashtriya Janata Dal, Shiv Sena (UBT) and the Left parties, kept up the heat on the NDA over the issue. articles.title: In 2017, four artists paid $95,000 to save Nina Simone's childhood home from demolition; eight years later, a nearly $850,000 rehabilitation restored the three-room North Carolina house
articles.summary: Nina Simone’s 650 sq ft childhood home in Tryon, North Carolina, has been restored after sitting vacant and severely decayed for more than two decades.
articles.body: Nina Simone’s 650 sq ft childhood home in Tryon, North Carolina, has been restored after sitting vacant and severely decayed for more than two decades. The three-room house, where the legendary musician and civil rights activist lived with her family from 1933, was bought for $95,000 in 2017 by four Black artists. Its rehabilitation was completed last year, after nearly $850,000 was spent on materials, construction and engineering.According to The Guardian, the restored home is now painted white, while parts of its original structure have been retained. A piece of the home’s original rust-brown varnish has been placed in a shadow box on a mint-blue wall. A small section of the original Great Depression-era linoleum has also been preserved on the restored wooden floor.For Simone’s younger brother, Samuel Waymon, returning to the house after its restoration brought back memories of his childhood. The 81-year-old composer remembered playing organ inside the home and cooking with his mother on the potbelly stove. He was also happy to see a large tree from his childhood still standing in the yard.“It does conjure up wonderful tears of joy in my heart and in my eyes when I stand in that house, on the porch, going into the rooms where the stove is, and I’m saying, ‘Wow, this is actually real. The house is restored.' It’s like time travel,” Waymon said.Artists come together to protect Simone’s homeThe house came to the attention of contemporary artist Adam Pendleton in 2016 after a museum curator told him that it was for sale. Pendleton initially thought about finding someone else who could protect the property, but later decided to take action himself.He then approached fellow artists Rashid Johnson, Julie Mehretu and Ellen Gallagher. The four formed the collective Daydream Therapy LLC and bought the house in 2017.Pendleton said the group wanted to protect a place connected to Simone’s life and contribution to American culture. He recalled thinking when he first walked through the property after buying it- “This is where it all started for Nina, in this humble home.”The group later worked with the African American Cultural Heritage Action Fund (AACHAF), which developed a preservation strategy for the property.Restoring the 650 sq ft houseThe restoration team used an old family photograph and research into early 20th-century African American homes in North Carolina to understand how the house originally looked. They also examined materials from the foundation and roof for clues while developing the restoration plan.The work included repairing the entryways and walls, evening out the floors and adding an accessible ramp. The aim was to improve the house while retaining its basic structure and connection to its past.In 2020, the AACHAF created a preservation easement for the property. The legal agreement restricts future changes to the site and prevents its demolition. Preservation North Carolina will oversee the historic protection of the home.The complete rehabilitation, which began in June 2024, was finished last year with the project involing nearly $850,000 in materials, construction and engineering costs.Home expected to open to public soonThe AACHAF is now working with a consulting team and the Tryon community on a long-term management and programming plan for the property. The home is projected to open to the public for tourism in 2027.The group also hopes to develop a cultural district around the house. Future plans include working with St Luke’s CME Church, where Simone’s mother, Kate Waymon, preached, to involve the surrounding East Side neighbourhood in programming.Pendleton has said he wants the house to become a place where artists can work with intention, including writing music or performing in the town. The project also received support from the Mellon and Tejemos foundations.For Waymon, however, the significance of the restoration remains deeply personal. He said the decision to preserve the house allowed visitors to experience the place where his sister spent part of her childhood.The restored home will also remain connected to Simone’s music. Waymon is releasing a new duet with his sister in January 2026 for the song “Love Me or Leave Me”. Simone’s voice was recorded in 1957, while Waymon added his part decades later.You use AI every day. articles.title: Beyond condoms: WHO blueprint for new male contraceptives
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Men could have more contraceptive choices beyond condoms and vasectomy, with the World Health Organization (WHO) releasing its first global
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Men could have more contraceptive choices beyond condoms and vasectomy, with the World Health Organization (WHO) releasing its first global blueprint for developing novel male contraceptives, including daily pills or gels, longer-acting injections and implants, sperm-function blockers and reversible methods that block sperm transport.The WHO's Target Product Profiles (TPPs) do not approve or launch any new contraceptive. Instead, they set minimum and optimal standards for the effectiveness, safety, reversibility, acceptability and affordability of future male contraceptives. The framework covers three approaches: suppressing sperm production, inhibiting sperm function and blocking sperm transmission or transport.The move comes as research into male contraception gathers pace, with several candidates already in clinical trials. RISUG (reversible inhibition of sperm under guidance), developed in India, has completed Phase 1 and Phase 2 studies, while another hydrogel-based method, ADAM, is in Phase 1 trials. Hormonal candidates including nestorone/testosterone gel, dimethandrolone undecanoate (DMAU) and 11β-methyl-19-nortestosterone dodecylcarbonate (11β-MNTDC) are also being investigated.For methods that suppress sperm production, WHO's minimum target is for 90% of men to achieve sperm concentrations of 1 million or fewer sperm per millilitre within 12 weeks, with a 12-month cumulative pregnancy rate of no more than 7%. The optimal target is 95% achieving this level within eight weeks, with the pregnancy rate at 3% or less.The proposed methods include daily tablets or gels, injections every three, six or 12 months and implants lasting at least a year. WHO's optimal profile also calls for sperm concentrations to return to the normal reference range within six months of stopping treatment.Another strategy is to leave sperm present but disable functions needed for fertilisation, such as motility and capacitation. A third is to block sperm transport through the vas deferens, potentially using reversible hydrogels, or temporarily block ejaculation with medication.WHO said the field is rapidly progressing, with several candidates in advanced clinical trials. The new profiles are intended to provide developers and regulators with a common framework for bringing future male contraceptives through research and development.You use AI every day. Further calling for action against terorrism, the EAM said, ""A persistent threat to peace has been the scourge of terrorism. That this could be state-sponsored, with cross-border purpose, makes it a direct affront to the global order. Governments indulging in such practices must be held accountable. Its financial aspects, in particular, should be exposed and should be countered."Jaishnakar further defended India's right to call out terrorism saying, "Friendship and goodwill cannot coexist with terrorism. articles.title: J&K BJP bigwig meets Shah day after Omar moves statehood resolution with autonomy reference
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: A day after CM Omar Abdullah moved an assembly resolution for restoration of J&K’s statehood with a reference to a similar document of the year
articles.body: SRINAGAR: A day after CM Omar Abdullah moved an assembly resolution for restoration of J&K’s statehood with a reference to a similar document of the year 2000 on autonomy, BJP leader of opposition Sunil Sharma met Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday for “advice” even as PDP upped the ante and sought an amendment to condemn Article 370’s abrogation.Vowing to block the resolution, Sharma said Shah “reaffirmed the Union govt’s unwavering commitment to peace, development and prosperity of Jammu and Kashmir”.Sharma made it clear that BJP was prepared to debate the statehood restoration document brought by the Omar-led National Conference (NC) govt but would not accept attempts to “smuggle in” issues of Article 370 and the 2000 autonomy resolution.“When the (Omar-led) govt has lost its strength on governance, an attempt is being made to recover that by invoking references designed to stir emotion among the people of Kashmir. At no cost will the so-called autonomy resolution or Article 370 be allowed to become part of this debate,” Sharma said.PDP would have none of it. It called Friday’s resolution “weak” and demanded that the document begin with a denunciation of Article 370’s revocation by the Centre on Aug 5, 2019. PDP legislator Muntazir Mehdi disclosed that he had moved an amendment calling on the House to “express its deep anguish over the unilateral measures” of 2019 and urging the Centre to ensure “immediate restoration of J&K’s full statehood along with its constitutional safeguards”.Omar had moved the resolution amid a BJP backlash to the autonomy reference, with its members ripping up copies amid anti-national chants directed at NC. MLAs of NC ally Congress supported the resolution and confronted rivals. CPM, Peoples Conference and PDP also backed the resolution. The autonomy resolution was passed by the assembly in June 2000 when J&K was a state.Explaining the reference to previous resolutions, Omar said the aim was to convey that the House continued to stand by all past decisions. He rejected BJP’s charges, asked “how demanding statehood can be anti-national” and pointed out that statehood was a promise made by the Centre and reaffirmed by PM Narendra Modi at an event where BJP’s Sharma was present.Omar has been under pressure for months now, accused by rivals of dropping demands to restore Article 370 and demanding statehood only. On Saturday, NC spokesperson Tanvir called the resolution a powerful reminder that the party had “not forgotten” its agenda. BJP MLA Devyani Rana accused NC of raking up 25-year-old autonomy demands on the pretext of statehood.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: Seoul became the setting for an unique architectural experiment in 2025, where a public installation was made from mushroom mycelium and agricultural waste instead of conventional building materials. Named as Walls of Public Life, the project was created by Mumbai-based Anomalia for the 5th Seoul Biennale of Architecture and Urbanism. Its blocks were grown using fungal networks that bind crop waste together, turning discarded organic material into lightweight building components. The installation offered a different way of thinking about walls, showing how some future construction materials could be cultivated rather than manufactured.Seoul’s mycelium walls turn mushroom waste into architectureThe Walls of Public Life installation was created for the first outdoor exhibition of the Seoul Biennale, held at Songhyeon Green Plaza. According to Anomalia’s project website, the studio was invited to create one of 24 Walls of Public Life for the 2025 event, curated by Thomas Heatherwick. The project explored what building facades could become if they were grown from mushroom mycelium rather than produced entirely through conventional industrial processes.The material at the centre of the installation was mycelium, the root-like network of fungi. Instead of treating agricultural waste as something to discard, the project used it as the main growing material. Crop waste was mixed with mycelium cultures, allowing the fungal network to spread through the organic material and naturally hold it together.This gave the waste a new purpose. Anomalia states that each block used 2.1 kilograms of crop waste while weighing about 1.5 kilograms. The resulting material could then be shaped into architectural components without relying on the energy-intensive processes normally associated with many conventional construction materials.The wall was grown through a low-energy processThe production method was relatively straightforward. Once the crop waste and mycelium cultures were combined, the mixture was placed into moulds. The fungal network grew through the material and acted as a natural binding system. The blocks were then dried and stabilised, producing the components used for the Seoul installation.Architecture Lab, in its report on Walls of Public Life, describes the installation as being made from MycoBlox and Biobo panels, which are mycelium-based materials combined with agricultural byproducts. The fungal networks bind the organic material as they grow, producing lightweight components with significant compressive strength.Anomalia’s own account gives the blocks a tested compressive capacity of up to 1.5 tons. That detail is important because the project was not simply about making an unusual surface from mushrooms. It was also an attempt to demonstrate that materials grown from biological processes could have practical qualities suitable for architectural use.What made the facade different from an ordinary wallThe installation was designed to look and behave differently from the sealed surfaces commonly found on buildings. Its porous structure allowed air and light to pass through, while its uneven texture created a surface that could be experienced through touch as well as sight.MYCL, the Indonesian material company involved in the research and production, describes the installation as a breathable and interactive facade. Its account says the MycoBlox provided 3D modular blocks, while the square BIBO panels created another layer within the structure.Instead of functioning simply as a solid division between people and their surroundings, the installation was intended to create a more open relationship between the structure, visitors and the surrounding environment.The project connected Mumbai, Bandung and SeoulThe unique wall was also the result of work spread across three countries. According to Anomalia, the design was developed in Mumbai, India, while the materials were grown in Bandung, Indonesia, in collaboration with MYCL. The finished components were then transported to South Korea and assembled at Songhyeon Green Plaza in Seoul.MYCL similarly describes the project as a cross-border collaboration between architectural design and material research. Its production model avoided the idea that every part of a building material has to come from a conventional high-heat manufacturing facility.The collaboration also brought together different areas of expertise. Anomalia handled design and research, while MYCL worked on material research and production. The project was supported by the Seoul Metropolitan Government and P4G(Partnering for Green Growth and the Global Goals 2030).What could grown building materials offer future architectureThe Seoul installation presented mycelium materials as biodegradable and carbon negative. MYCL describes that the materials were designed to return to the earth at the end of their useful life.Another feature was the use of a modular wooden framework. MYCL notes that the framework allowed the installation to be disassembled, supporting a more circular approach to construction rather than treating the structure as something permanently fixed in place.Architecture Lab describes Walls of Public Life as a practical test of mycelium composite blocks in an outdoor public setting, where the material faced rain, storms, humidity and regular human interaction.You use AI every day. articles.title: Three siblings in Essex cut down their neighbours’ 33-foot Leylandii trees after a boundary row; the dispute ended with about £30,500 in damages and £178,668 in the neighbours’ legal costs
articles.summary: Three siblings in Essex were ordered to pay about £30,500 in damages and £178,668 in their neighbours’ legal costs after cutting down a row of 33-foot
articles.body: Three siblings in Essex were ordered to pay about £30,500 in damages and £178,668 in their neighbours’ legal costs after cutting down a row of 33-foot Leylandii trees during a long-running boundary dispute. The court found that the siblings had trespassed into their neighbours’ garden and acted in a 'high-handed' and 'bullying' manner.According to The Standard, the dispute involved Robert McCarthy, 59, his wife Amanda, 61, and their neighbours Foulla Bowler, 61, John Barberis, 63, and Mary Englishby, 59. The McCarthys had lived in their home in Nazeing, Essex, since 2001, while Bowler had grown up in the neighbouring family home, which she now owns with her brother and sister.The two properties were separated by a fence, with a line of Leylandii trees on the McCarthys’ side. But around 2018, a dispute began over where the actual boundary between the gardens lay. Bowler and her siblings claimed the boundary was beyond the fence and that the trees therefore stood on their land.The disagreement eventually led to the removal of the fence and the cutting down of most of the trees in January 2022. The McCarthys said the loss of the trees left their garden exposed, damaged their privacy and changed how they used their home. They later took the siblings to court.Dispute turns into court battleThe court heard that the McCarthys believed the old fence marked the boundary when they bought their home. Robert McCarthy said the trees were already well established at the time.“The trees were well-established when we moved in,” he told the judge, as quoted by The Standard. “We thought the chain link fence was the boundary as it ran along. I had no reason not to believe that to be the boundary,” McCarthy added.The siblings, however, maintained that the fence and trees were actually on their land. They said they had the right to remove them because they were causing 'overshadowing' and could potentially damage their property.The dispute continued for several years. Bowler had applied in 2018 for permission to fell 29 trees. According to the McCarthys’ barrister, Christopher Coyle, the family later went ahead with the removal, with the felling continuing into a second day even after the McCarthys’ lawyers had written to ask them to stop.Robert McCarthy described the work as an “invasion” and said it had resulted in a “relentless destruction of my garden. This is how we feel as a family. I can stand upstairs in my house and they can see me walking around. I want my privacy back like I had,” he told the court.Couple said they stopped using their gardenThe McCarthys told the court that the removal of the trees had affected their family’s everyday life. They said they no longer felt comfortable using the back garden and had stopped inviting people, including their children’s friends, to their home.Amanda McCarthy said they had “only ever used the front rooms of their house” since the trees were removed. She also told the court that she had become “depressed as a result of the stress that has been caused”.“After the invasion it feels completely destroyed. There's little or nothing left of what was our garden. Since the invasion we don't use the garden at all,” she said.The couple had sought compensation that included the cost of planting new trees and restoring their privacy. They also asked the court to declare that the true boundary was the line of the old fence.In an earlier judgment following a trial, Judge Alan Saggerson ruled in favour of the McCarthys on the location of the boundary. He found that the siblings had trespassed into the neighbours’ garden when they removed the trees.The judge said the siblings had taken “unilateral action to re-order the disputed boundary” during what he described as “fence wars” between the neighbours.He also said their evidence was less reliable and less accurate than that of the McCarthys. However, he did not find that the siblings were lying. Instead, he said they had “persuaded themselves of the righteousness of their own case.”Judge orders damages and legal costsAt a further hearing this week, Judge Saggerson ordered the siblings to pay around £30,500 in damages and £178,668 towards the McCarthys’ legal costs. The amount comes on top of the siblings’ own court costs.The judge said the cutting down of the trees had caused a trespass and had a serious effect on the McCarthys’ use of their property.“The centre of gravity in this case is the cutting down of trees on or around the border, which in my judgment caused a trespass and had a serious impact on the claimants’ amenity in a number of ways. It opened up their rear garden to the unwanted attention of their neighbours,” he said.The judge also referred to “unfortunate acrimonious shouting and terms of abuse being hurled from the defendants’ garden into the claimants’ garden”. He said the couple had stopped inviting people round and that their children had particularly stopped inviting friends.“The loss of privacy was significant in a domestic situation such as this. From January 2022 I accept that the claimants had to live more and more, almost exclusively, at the front of their house,” he said.The judge further said the situation had a detrimental effect on Amanda McCarthy’s mental health. He also criticised the siblings’ “aggressive and somewhat bullying behaviour”. “It seems clear to me that the claimants have been victimised by high-handed oppressive behaviour. It goes way beyond the ordinary course of trespass,” he said.£105,000 tree replacement rejectedThe McCarthys had sought enough money to replace the removed trees with new trees measuring about 8 metres tall. That work was estimated to cost £105,000.Judge Saggerson refused to award that amount. He said, “No reasonable person spending their own money would do this,” and instead awarded the couple £5,000 for smaller trees that could be planted and allowed to grow.The judge also noted that the siblings’ property was being marketed, or was expected to be marketed. Following the ruling, the three siblings are selling their childhood home, according to the court hearing.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Tenth woman's body found in South Africa suburb as police probe killings
articles.summary: The deaths have sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in the country.
articles.body:
Police in South Africa say that they have discovered another body in a Johannesburg suburb, bringing the number of women found dead there in recent months to ten.

The body was found on Saturday morning and was identified by the friend with whom she had been at a bar the previous evening.

The local police commissioner said his force could not rule out the possibility that there was a serial killer on the loose, noting similarities across the 10 deaths in Ekurhuleni, as well as another in Soweto.

The deaths have sparked a national outcry about the scale of violence against women in the country, which has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world.

The latest body was discovered at a cemetery in the Tembisa neighbourhood north-east of central Johannesburg.

Police issued a statement a short while later saying crime scene investigators were at the scene gathering evidence. Officials have yet to publicly identify the victim.

The woman's friend told national broadcaster SABC that she recognised her friend's clothes from the previous night when shown a picture of the body.

"I don't know what I'm going to say to her children," she said while wiping away tears. "It's painful."

Gauteng Police Commissioner Tommy Mthombeni said that, at this early stage in the investigation, it was too soon to say whether the woman's death was linked to the others.

He told reporters that the other bodies shared a "similar victimology" that indicated a shared "modus operandi" of killing, which would allow police to determine whether this latest death was linked to the others.

"For now, it's not something which we can overrule to say there's a serial killer, but we cannot conclusively indicate as such," Lt Gen Mthombeni said.

South Africa has one of the highest homicide rates, with 5,427 people murdered between April and June this year alone.

But it is the nature of the recent killings around Johannesburg that has left many women there reeling from the growing death toll.

The 10 other bodies have been found in similar circumstances to one another since July. Most of them were found in Kempton Park, one neighbourhood over from Tembisa.

Many of the bodies were those of young women and almost all had suffered extreme violence prior to their deaths.

The deaths have increased pressure on the national government less than a year after ministers declared gender-based violence a national disaster.

While South African police statistics do not differentiate victims by gender, the South African Human Rights Commission said last week that 569 women were killed and 1,052 others survived attempted murder between April and June this year.

Three men appeared in court earlier this week accused of being involved in one of the nine murders, with police working to track down others who may have been involved.

articles.title: Meet Jessica Lee, 17-year old Honolulu high school senior who logged 420 hours of volunteer service, competed in varsity golf and completed a multi-day expedition before earning the US Congress’s highest youth award
articles.summary: For 17-year-old Jessica Lee, earning the highest youth honor presented by the U.S. Congress was not the result of a single achievement.
articles.body: For 17-year-old Jessica Lee, earning the highest youth honor presented by the U.S. Congress was not the result of a single achievement. It came from hundreds of hours spent serving her community, years on the golf course, music rehearsals, an expedition and a determination to keep learning outside the classroom. The Punahou School senior from Honolulu received the Congressional Award Gold Medal in August, joining 877 young people across the country recognized with the honor this year, states the Aloha State Daily.420 hours serving her communityFor the uninitiated, the Congressional Award Gold Medal recognizes young people who complete a demanding two-year program covering voluntary public service, personal development, physical fitness and an expedition or exploration. Recipients must complete at least 400 hours of voluntary public service, 200 hours of personal development, 200 hours of physical fitness and a five-day, four-night expedition. Lee exceeded the service requirement with 420 hours of volunteer work, much of it connected to health care and older adults. Her interest in the medical field was shaped in part by her grandfather's experience with lung cancer in Korea. His difficulties navigating diagnosis and treatment, including misinformation, influenced Lee's interest in health literacy and patient advocacy.At St. Francis Healthcare System of Hawaiʻi, she spent time with elderly patients, interacted with medical professionals and observed health-care settings firsthand. She also saw how language barriers could make it difficult for some families to understand medical information and participate fully in decisions about their care.Turning health advocacy into actionLee eventually founded the Cancer Health Awareness & Mindfulness Program, or CHAMP, a nonprofit focused on improving health literacy. Through the program, she organizes workshops covering cancer risks, prevention and local resources. CHAMP also partnered with the University of Hawaiʻi Cancer Center Skin Van for a skin cancer awareness event at Ala Moana Beach Park. Her community work extends to Punahou, where she helps lead Caring of the Elderly, a program serving kūpuna in Mānoa twice each month.A state champion on the golf courseOutside her volunteer work, Lee has spent much of her life on the golf course. She began playing at age 4 after her family moved from New York to Hawaiʻi. She competes on Punahou's Varsity I girls golf team, which won the state championship three consecutive years. Lee also finished second in the state in 2024. Golf became another part of her personal-development journey, demanding discipline while teaching her to recover from mistakes and keep moving through difficult rounds.Music, travel and cultural advocacyLee's interests extend well beyond medicine and athletics. She began playing violin in fourth grade and joined her school's orchestra the following year, developing an appreciation for different musical repertoires. A spring 2025 trip to Boston added another challenge. She toured college campuses, visited museums and explored the city, navigating public transportation and the subway for the first time.Her advocacy for Korean heritage has also been a long-running project. Beginning in seventh grade, Lee pushed for greater inclusion of Korean language and heritage in school curricula. She created a petition signed by 300 students and brought the issue to neighborhood boards and the Hawaiʻi Legislature.Looking toward medicineCongressman Ed Case presented Lee with her Gold Medal and a certificate of special recognition in August. She became the seventh person from his district to receive the honor over the past 25 years. Now, as she applies to colleges, Lee is looking toward a future at the intersection of public health and culture. Her goal is to become a physician while continuing to focus on health literacy and helping patients better understand their medical choices. For a teenager balancing school, sport, music, advocacy and hundreds of volunteer hours, the Congressional Award marks less a finish line than a record of what she has already built, and a foundation for the work ahead.Images Courtesy: Congressman Ed CaseYou use AI every day. articles.title: Who is Christos Marafatsos, the Greek-American businessman accompanying Kimberly Guilfoyle to key meetings?
articles.summary: US Ambassador to Greece and Donald Trump Jr's ex Kimberly Guilfoyle has come under scrutiny over the prominent role played by Greek-American businessman
articles.body: US Ambassador to Greece and Donald Trump Jr's ex Kimberly Guilfoyle has come under scrutiny over the prominent role played by Greek-American businessman and lobbyist Christos Marafatsos during her efforts to promote US energy interests across southeastern Europe. A Wall Street Journal investigation reported that Marafatsos, 39, has frequently accompanied Guilfoyle to high-level meetings despite having no official role in the US government. He is a registered lobbyist for Greek construction company Aktor Group, which has expanded into the natural gas business.The report said some foreign officials who encountered Marafatsos alongside Guilfoyle assumed he was a member of her official diplomatic team or even her chief of staff. In reality, he is a private businessman whose lobbying work includes representing Aktor.Why is Marafatsos accompanying Guilfoyle?Guilfoyle has been travelling across the Balkans to promote a proposed "vertical gas corridor", an infrastructure network intended to bring US liquefied natural gas (LNG) into Greece and move it north towards countries including Ukraine.During a visit to Bulgaria, Guilfoyle reportedly encouraged officials to work with Aktor. Marafatsos was present during a meeting with Bulgaria's president.The Journal reported that Aktor's chief executive had flown Guilfoyle to Bulgaria on a private jet. Several people who attended meetings involving Guilfoyle and Marafatsos told the newspaper that Marafatsos did not disclose his relationship with Aktor during those meetings.Aktor registered Marafatsos as a lobbyist in November, shortly after Guilfoyle arrived in Athens. Federal lobbying records cited by the Journal show that the company paid him $160,000 through June to help establish connections with the White House, State Department and Energy Department.Who is Christos Marafatsos?Marafatsos was raised in Maryland and has worked in several businesses, including a produce distribution company in the Washington area, real estate consulting and a venture involving an IMAX 3D attraction focused on the Acropolis.His political connections predate Guilfoyle's appointment as ambassador. He became involved in Donald Trump's political operation during Trump's first presidential campaign and later chaired Greek Voices for Trump.After Trump nominated Guilfoyle as ambassador to Greece, Marafatsos reportedly helped prepare her for her Senate confirmation hearing and attended her swearing-in.Trump has also publicly acknowledged Marafatsos. During a Greek Independence Day event at the White House, Trump pointed him out and described him as a "good looking guy".What does Guilfoyle's team say?Guilfoyle's lawyer, Jesse Binnall, rejected the suggestion that the ambassador was improperly promoting one company. He said Guilfoyle has worked with companies across the energy sector and that her official meetings are arranged through embassy channels.Secretary of State Marco Rubio has described Guilfoyle as an effective advocate for the administration's agenda.Marafatsos said he was proud to promote commercial initiatives that he believes advance US interests and create economic opportunities in Greece and southeastern Europe.Aktor's lawyers also disputed the suggestion that the company's involvement in the energy corridor resulted from Guilfoyle's intervention, saying its participation began before any contacts with the ambassador.You use AI every day. articles.title: Two get life sentence for murder over land dispute in 2010
articles.summary: Sultanpur court sentences brothers Girish and Satish Pandey to life for 2010 land dispute murder of Ayodhya Bakhsh Singh; ₹1.54 lakh fine, ₹1 lakh to family.
articles.body: Lucknow: A Sultanpur court has sentenced two brothers to life imprisonment for the murder of a man, Ayodhya Bakhsh Singh, who was shot dead in 2010 during a dispute over alleged encroachment on residential land.District and sessions judge Sunil Kumar on Friday sentenced Girish Kumar Pandey and his brother Satish Pandey to life imprisonment and imposed a combined fine of Rs 1.54 lakh on them.The court directed that ₹1 lakh from the fine should be paid to the victim’s family as compensation.On July 30, 2010, Jitendra Singh, a resident of Nohrepur-Raghunathpur village under the Munshiganj police station area of Amethi, lodged an FIR after the killing of his father.According to the prosecution, Girish Kumar Pandey, a retired head constable, and his family members were allegedly attempting to take possession of a piece of residential land and merge it with their agricultural field. The dispute escalated when the victim’s family objected to the alleged encroachment.The prosecution told the court that Girish Pandey opened fire with his licensed rifle, killing Ayodhya Bakhsh. When his son Ravindra Singh tried to intervene, he was allegedly attacked with the rifle butt and injured.Based on Jitendra Singh’s complaint, police registered a case against Girish Pandey, his brother Satish Pandey and their relative Vineet Pandey under sections related to murder and other offences. After completing the investigation, police filed a charge sheet before the court.A cross-FIR was also registered on behalf of Girish Pandey against the deceased’s sons, Jitendra and Ravindra, alleging an attempt to kill. However, the court acquitted Jitendra and Ravindra in the cross-case for lack of sufficient evidence.The court had convicted Girish and Satish on Wednesday in the murder case and on Friday pronounced the quantum of sentence. Both were ordered to be sent back to jail to serve their life sentences.During the trial, accused Vineet Pandey died, and proceedings against him consequently came to an end.The prosecution examined eight witnesses during the trial. The prosecution was represented by the in charge district govt counsel (criminal), who argued that the testimony of the witnesses and other evidence established the charges against the two surviving accused.After the sentencing, Ravindra Singh, son of the deceased, said his family had finally received justice after 16 years.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Lucknow | Silver Rate in Lucknow | Bank Holidays in Lucknow | Public Holidays in Lucknow | Lucknow AQI | Weather in Lucknow | Petrol Price in Lucknow | Diesel Price in Lucknow | CNG Price in Lucknow | LPG Price in LucknowStay updated with the latest Lucknow news. articles.title: What do the latest US visa wait times reveal: Hyderabad, Mumbai near a year for B1/B2 appointments; Delhi at 10 months
articles.summary: Indian applicants seeking US visitor visas continue to face lengthy waits, with the latest US State Department data showing next available B-1/B-2
articles.body: Indian applicants seeking US visitor visas continue to face lengthy waits, with the latest US State Department data showing next available B-1/B-2 interview appointments stretching to 12 months in Hyderabad, 11.5 months in Mumbai and 10 months in New Delhi.The State Department updated its global visa wait-time data on September 17, with the figures showing significant differences between visitor visa and student visa appointment availability at US consular posts in India.Hyderabad has longest B-1/B-2 waitHyderabad recorded an average B-1/B-2 interview wait of 11.5 months, while the next available appointment was listed at 12 months.Mumbai's average wait stood at 11 months, with the next available appointment at 11.5 months.At the US Embassy in New Delhi, the average B-1/B-2 wait was 7.5 months, while the next available appointment was listed at 10 months.Chennai recorded an average wait of seven months, with the next available B-1/B-2 appointment at 7.5 months.The figures represent estimates rather than guarantees. The State Department says US embassies and consulates regularly release additional appointment slots, meaning applicants may be able to obtain an earlier date after booking an appointment.Student visa appointments remain much shorterThe situation is considerably different for applicants seeking F, M and J visas.In Chennai, the next available appointment was listed at less than half a month. Hyderabad had a wait of 1.5 months, while Mumbai stood at 2.5 months and New Delhi at two months.Work visa appointment waits varyApplicants for petition-based H, L, O, P and Q visas also saw differences across Indian posts.The next available appointment was listed at 1.5 months in Chennai, 5.5 months in Hyderabad, 1.5 months in Mumbai and three months in New Delhi.For Indian H-1B and other employment-based visa applicants, the figures are particularly relevant because the appointment availability varies sharply depending on the consular post.Mumbai backlog improves, Hyderabad worsensCompared with the previous month's data, the picture has shifted in opposite directions at some Indian posts.Mumbai's B-1/B-2 average wait fell from 14 months in August to 11 months in September, while Hyderabad's increased from 9.5 months to 11.5 months. New Delhi's average remained at 7.5 months.The next available B-1/B-2 appointment in Mumbai also improved from 14 months to 11.5 months. articles.title: Fake GST check turns into extortion bid on Hamirpur Highway, 4 held
articles.summary: Fake GST officers allegedly used e-way bill details to extort Rs 50,000 from a truck driver on Hamirpur Highway; 4 arrested, 2 absconding.
articles.body: Lucknow: A group of four men allegedly posed as GST officials, used details from a truck’s e-way bill and tax invoice to make their claims appear genuine, and demanded Rs 50,000 from the driver. What initially appeared to be a GST inspection on a highway in Hamirpur was later found to be an alleged extortion attempt, according to police.Hamirpur Police have arrested four people for allegedly posing as GST officials and stopping a vehicle carrying kitchen goods from Lucknow to Mahoba. Two other members of the group are on the run.The case came to light on Sept 22, when a vehicle carrying goods linked to former MP Gangacharan Rajput was stopped near the Hamirpur bypass at around 8 am. The men allegedly introduced themselves as GST officials and demanded Rs 50,000 from the driver.The driver was allegedly threatened, and Rs 11,000 in cash was also taken from his pocket, police said.The alleged scam began to unravel when the owner of the consignment, Suresh Chandra, sought to verify the purported GST inspection with the department.A state tax officer, Durgaprasad, checked the location and found that no authorised GST checking was taking place there.When the officer contacted the driver, he reportedly learnt that four to five men travelling in a Bolero had stopped the vehicle, claimed to be GST officials and demanded Rs 50,000.That call triggered the police investigation. Investigators say the alleged extortion attempt was not random.Police found that the vehicle owner, Mahesh Pandey, and driver Dinesh Singh had allegedly shared the truck’s e-way bill and tax invoice. The information was then allegedly used by Bhola Yadav alias Sunny and his associates to contact the consignment owner while posing as a GST official named Harshit Kumar from the Kanpur division.The suspects allegedly used details from the documents to make the fake inspection appear credible.Police recovered fake GST identity cards from Bhola Yadav and Aman Yadav during their arrests. Mobile phones and SIM cards allegedly used by the accused were also seized.During interrogation, police said they uncovered what they suspect was a wider modus operandi. SP, Hamirpur, Mrigank Shekhar Pathak, said that Bhola allegedly operated with his brother Sagar and associate Krishna. The group had reportedly earlier been involved in helping trucks move covertly across the Bihar border to evade GST checks.As border enforcement became stricter, police said, the suspects allegedly shifted tactics.They allegedly began gathering information about trucks and consignments through drivers and vehicle owners staying at dhabas and roadside hotels. articles.title: After Daunte Wright’s 2021 death, a GoFundMe raised about $1.04 million; a year later, the mother of his only child sued his parents and Ben Crump, alleging the boy received none of the money promised for his support
articles.summary: What began as a public effort to support Daunte Wright’s family after his death later became a dispute over more than $1 million in donations.
articles.body: What began as a public effort to support Daunte Wright’s family after his death later became a dispute over more than $1 million in donations. A GoFundMe campaign launched following Wright’s fatal shooting in Minnesota in 2021 raised $1,039,207 from nearly 29,000 donors. But in October 2022, Chyna Whitaker, the mother of Wright’s only child, filed a lawsuit alleging that her son had been promised a share of the money but received none. The Minnesota court complaint alleged that half of the fundraiser proceeds had been promised to the child.How the $1 million fundraiser beganDaunte Wright, 20, was fatally shot by former Brooklyn Center police officer Kim Potter during a traffic stop on April 11, 2021. His death prompted an outpouring of public attention and support for his family. A GoFundMe campaign called the “Daunte Wright Sr. Memorial Fund” was created after his death. Kelly Bryant, Wright’s aunt, was listed as the organiser, while Arbuey Wright was named as the beneficiary. The campaign set a fundraising goal of $1.1 million. According to the GoFundMe page, it ultimately collected $1,039,207 through nearly 29,000 donations.The campaign described several intended uses for the money, including funeral and burial expenses, mental health and grief counselling, family support and efforts to seek justice following Wright’s death. The lawsuit also said the fundraiser referred to Wright’s infant son and that the money would help support him and the wider family.What Wright’s son’s mother allegedThe legal dispute surfaced about 18 months after the fundraiser was launched. Chyna Whitaker, who was the mother of Wright’s only child, filed a civil lawsuit in Minnesota state court on October 3, 2022. According to the complaint, Whitaker alleged that she had been assured that 50% of the GoFundMe proceeds would go to her son, Daunte Wright Jr. The lawsuit calculated that amount at approximately $519,495, based on the total raised by the campaign.Whitaker alleged that she relied on those assurances when making decisions about financial support for her son. She claimed that she believed the existing fundraiser would provide for him and therefore did not establish a separate fundraising campaign. The complaint also named attorney Ben Crump and alleged that he had made or communicated assurances concerning the distribution of the funds. Whitaker sought damages exceeding $500,000 and brought claims including breach of contract and fraud and misrepresentation. These claims were allegations contained in the complaint and should not be treated as court findings.What the GoFundMe page saidAccording to the GoFundMe page, donations would help the Wright family with funeral and burial costs, mental health and grief counselling, family support and efforts to seek justice. It also mentioned Wright’s son and the need to support him following his father's death. However, the page also stated that the funds would be transferred to an account designated by Wright’s parents. It said the parents would manage and spend the money and described them as having ownership rights over the funds collected. This became significant because Whitaker's lawsuit alleged that she had separately been promised a specific share for her son.The dispute therefore involved a question about how the public fundraising language interacted with the alleged private assurances concerning the child's financial benefit.Ben Crump and Wright’s parents named as defendantsWhitaker's lawsuit named Wright’s parents and Ben Crump as defendants. The complaint alleged that representations were made about the money and that Whitaker understood those representations to mean her son would receive a substantial portion of the fundraiser proceeds. FOX 9 reported on the lawsuit when it was filed, including Whitaker's effort to obtain money from the fundraiser for her son. The case was therefore centred on the alleged promises surrounding the donations and whether those promises created an obligation to provide Wright’s son with a particular portion of the money.The separate $3.25 million settlementThe GoFundMe dispute was separate from another major financial matter connected to Wright’s death. In 2022, the City of Brooklyn Center agreed to a $3.25 million settlement with Wright’s family. The settlement was not part of the GoFundMe campaign. It resulted from a separate legal matter involving the city and Wright’s family.The distribution of that settlement was subsequently reviewed by a court. According to FOX 9, a judge approved a distribution plan under which Daunte Wright Jr. was set to receive more than $2 million from the settlement. The distinction is important because the $1.04 million fundraiser came from individual public donations, while the $3.25 million represented a separate settlement with the city.Why the case drew attentionThe dispute illustrates the complications that can arise when large public fundraisers are created following a death and different people have different understandings about how the money will be used. In Wright’s case, nearly 29,000 people donated more than $1 million through a campaign that described support for his family and young son. The fundraiser also gave Wright’s parents control over the account and the collected funds. Whitaker's lawsuit alleged that she had been given separate assurances that half of the money would belong to her son.The October 2022 complaint placed those competing claims before a Minnesota court. At the centre of the dispute was not whether the fundraiser had raised the money, but what donors had been told, what promises were allegedly made and who was ultimately entitled to the proceeds.You use AI every day. articles.title: Who is Cath Bowie? Meet the grandmother who became Fortnite’s oldest Twitch streamer and Guinness World Record holder
articles.summary: Cath Bowie is a 78-year-old grandmother from the United Kingdom who has turned her love for Fortnite into a successful Twitch streaming journey.
articles.body: Cath Bowie is a 78-year-old grandmother from the United Kingdom who has turned her love for Fortnite into a successful Twitch streaming journey. Known online as grumpygran1948, Bowie recently earned a Guinness World Records title for her work as a Fortnite streamer. Her gaming story began when she watched her grandson play Fortnite and became curious about the game. What started as something she watched from the side soon became a new passion. Today, she has built a loyal online community and continues to stream the game.Who is Cath Bowie, the 78-year-old Fortnite streamer?Cath Bowie did not start out as a gamer. Her journey began when she watched her grandson play Fortnite. She became interested in what he was doing and soon wanted to try the game herself.Speaking to Guinness World Records, Bowie said she was “immediately hooked” after watching the game.She then picked up a controller and started playing. Before long, she decided to take another big step and begin streaming her games online.Her grandson did not think many people would watch her. Instead of giving up, Bowie used his doubt as motivation.“As a young guy, he just couldn’t believe that his grandma would do such a thing and suggested that nobody would join me or watch me,” she told Guinness World Records. “Saying that was like a red rag to a bull to me. I would show him that I could do it.”Bowie started her Twitch channel in 2017 under the name grumpygran1948. The name was suggested by her granddaughter and became the identity that many viewers came to know.Over the years, she built a community of more than 24,000 people around her streams. Her story also shows that gaming and livestreaming are not only for young people.How Cath Bowie became a Guinness World Record holderBowie’s years of playing and streaming Fortnite eventually brought her international recognition. After celebrating her 78th birthday on September 1, she officially earned a Guinness World Records title connected to her Fortnite streaming career.The achievement made Bowie an example of how a person can discover a completely new passion at any age.Her love for streaming has also remained strong. Bowie said she has continued to enjoy playing and livestreaming throughout the years.“Most importantly, throughout all these years, I have continued to enjoy every day, every week, every month, and every year that I have played and live-streamed,” she said.Bowie also thanked her family and the friends she made through gaming. She encouraged other people not to let their age stop them from trying something new.“Never let age hold you back. If I could do it, so can you,” Bowie said.Cath Bowie’s journey from watching her grandson play Fortnite to becoming a Guinness World Record holder is a remarkable streaming story. At 78, she continues to play, stream, and connect with people through Twitch. Her story also proves that a new hobby can become something much bigger when someone is willing to give it a try.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Buoyed by the Election Commission's statement, BJP Saturday said it has exposed Congress and its allies as their attack on the poll body was nothing but a continuation of their tactic of shifting blame for their shrinking popular support in elections and demanded their apology.BJP president Nitin Nabin said, "Opposition has once again been exposed for misleading the public on SIR. articles.title: California construction workers uncover 40-million-year-old fossils; they could belong to extinct 'thunder beast' or 'swamp rhino'
articles.summary: Workers on a routine infrastructure project in Oceanside, California, recently uncovered the fossilised remains of a large, hoofed mammal that lived tens
articles.body: Workers on a routine infrastructure project in Oceanside, California, recently uncovered the fossilised remains of a large, hoofed mammal that lived tens of millions of years ago. The significant find, which included several limb bones, ribs and numerous other bones and fragments, was uncovered approximately 12 feet below the surface during routine excavation for a city infrastructure project, according to the City of Oceanside. A palaeontologist now believes the bones belong to one of two extinct, rhino-sized mammals that roamed North America during the Eocene Epoch.Why the fossils were unearthed during routine monitoring of a construction projectJoseph El Adli, PhD, the city's principal palaeontologist, discovered the site during routine monitoring and immediately secured the area to begin additional excavation. The city has kept the exact location under wraps; other outlets that covered the release reported this is meant to protect the site from unauthorised digging that could damage further fossils still in the ground.His team worked over a period of seven days to expose the fossil bones from beneath several tons of hardened mudstone and sandstone before encasing them in a plaster field jacket for safe transport to an off-site laboratory for eventual preparation.Could the bones belong to a rhino-sized 'thunder beast'Based on the size and shape of the bones uncovered during the excavation, Dr El Adli believes they likely belonged to an animal from one of two extinct mammal families that once roamed North America, both of which belong within the order Perissodactyla, the odd-toed hoofed mammals.The first possibility is a brontothere, sometimes called a titanothere or "thunder beast." A brontothere is a massive, hoofed mammal with a deep chest, a pronounced hump at the shoulder and a distinctive Y-shaped bony horn on the nose. They were land-dwelling creatures that fed on soft leaves and vegetation in forested habitats. The particular species known from this rock formation was roughly the size of a modern black rhino.The second possibility is an amynodont, historically referred to as a "swamp rhino." Amynodon had hornless faces and squat, hippopotamus-like bodies, with low, barrel-shaped torsos, short sturdy legs, a broad flat skull, and tusk-like canine teeth rather than a horn. Some amynodons were semi-aquatic, spending much of their time wallowing in rivers, ponds, and lakes and grazing on coarse aquatic and streamside vegetation, while others were more lightly built and lived on land.What Member C of the Santiago Formation reveals about the fossils' Eocene-era ageThe bones were recovered from Member C of the Santiago Formation, a thick sequence of sedimentary rocks exposed across parts of northwestern San Diego County. The formation dates to the Eocene Epoch and has previously yielded fossils from that time period within the city, as well as elsewhere in the region. Based on the surrounding rock and known organisms from the formation, palaeontologists estimate the specimen lived roughly 40 to 45 million years ago.What happens next for the newly discovered Oceanside fossilsThe fossils, now encased in plaster field jackets, have been transported off-site for lab preparation. Other outlets that reviewed the city's release reported that technicians will eventually free the bones from their plaster jackets and the surrounding hardened mudstone, then stabilise them with glues and resins so they can be preserved, to eventually place them in a museum collection where scientists and the public can study them.You use AI every day.
